title: Matched 65k preflop-head-only contextual prior pilot
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: At 65k hands, the isolated contextual prior treatment will sustain healthier SB-open and BB-defense policies and improve untouched learned-anchor performance over a matched preflop-only PPO control, while postflop execution remains exactly frozen.
material_change: Train fresh matched 65,536-physical-hand preflop-head-only control/treatment arms from the frozen soup with new seed/deals, duplicate-soup plus 50% procedural rollouts, source KL 0.1, identical assignments and reset optimizer/counters. Treatment alone enables both validated contextual prior coefficients at 0.01.
baseline: The 8k isolated mechanism smoke passed all gates: BB raise 94.03% to 89.80%, SB raise 99.62% to 99.38%, postflop policy exact, overall parent TV 0.01245. No strength evidence yet; current best soup is -41.8162 fresh20k Slumbot.

notes: Preregistered endpoint: final iter after each arm first crosses 65,536 physical hands. Health requires both session audits PASS, exact source/pool hashes, identical normalized assignments, fresh optimizer/counters, zero KL stops, only preflop/value tensors changed, and bitwise parent postflop policy.

After health, replay source corpus outcome-blind and run untouched current-v6 mirrored 2,048 pairs per arm against each of Standard10, slumbot_free and corrected CFR96 using a new common-randomness seed. Consider exploratory matched fresh5k Slumbot only if treatment improves contextual target distance, keeps overall parent TV/disagreement <=0.05, pooled learned-panel delta >0, and is positive on at least 2/3 anchors. No 100k qualification from this pilot.
Control frozen at preregistered iter16 endpoint: 67,777 physical/65,853 transition hands, max displayed source KL 0.0023, zero stops.
Both iter16 fixed-pool session audits PASS with 16 archives/assignments, optimizer step454, exact source hashes and zero KL stops.

Outcome-blind corpus: postflop exactly preserved and contextual aggression corrected, but treatment-parent overall TV/disagreement 0.06377/0.08378 exceed the preregistered 0.05 Slumbot-allocation boundary. Slumbot allocation is therefore disallowed for iter16.

Independent terminal review PASS: hashes, 16-row assignment chains, both session audits, strict tensor scope, exact postflop preservation, 60,671 mechanism rows, all 6,144 learned-panel pair decks/rewards/CIs, and failed Slumbot allocation gate recomputed. 175 tests PASS.

result.summary: Matched 65k arms completed 135,641 physical hands. Treatment strongly reduced BB-vs-open raise frequency 92.68% to 46.71% and kept postflop policy exact, but exceeded preservation limits (overall parent TV/disagreement 0.06377/0.08378). Learned panel was inconclusive at +5.42 bb/100 CI[-28.40,39.24] with only 1/3 positive anchors.
result.conclusion: The isolated prior direction is mechanistically effective but coefficient 0.01 for 65k hands is an excessive dose. Iter16 fails both drift criteria and anchor-consistency, so it is rejected without Slumbot evaluation; the immutable checkpoint curve can identify an earlier safe dose without new training.
result.next_step: Open a separate outcome-blind dose-curve experiment over the archived matched checkpoints. Replay fixed source states at even iterations to find the latest treatment endpoint satisfying overall parent TV/disagreement <=0.05 with improved contextual target distance, then run a fresh untouched anchor panel only at that preregistered boundary checkpoint.
